cards.explanation: The answer is a dwelling place. Moses, Israel's leader, says “…You have been our dwelling place through all generations.” That's a home, and not just for one family but for everybody down the line. I once lived in a junk drawer, friends, and nobody would call that a dwelling place with a straight face.

The answer is True! The psalm says, “…from everlasting to everlasting You are God.” That covers the time before the mountains were born, and before He brought forth the earth and the world. There's no starting line on this one, friends. I can barely remember where I put my own apron.
The answer is dust! The verse says, “You return man to dust…” It's a plain, quiet line, and it sets up the picture of how short our days are. We'll watch the psalm keep building on that.

The answer is a day gone by. The psalm says a thousand years in His sight “…are but a day that passes, or a watch of the night.” A thousand years, and in His sight it's like a day passing. Meanwhile I get impatient when my first batch takes twelve minutes.

The answer is new grass! The psalm says people are “…like the new grass of the morning…” It's fresh and green at sunrise, and that's the picture Moses picks. Next verse, we find out what happens to it.

The answer is evening. The psalm says, “…in the morning it springs up new, but by evening it fades and withers.” The whole story fits inside one day. Up at sunrise and done by supper time, and I think that's exactly what Moses wants us to see.

The answer is our secret sins. The verse says, “You have set our iniquities before You, our secret sins in the light of Your presence.” Nothing is tucked away from Him. I think this one is heavy, friends, so it's okay to just sit with it a moment.

The answer is seventy or eighty years. The verse puts it this way: “The length of our days is seventy years—or eighty if we are strong…” It's a short window, friends. The verse goes on to say the days quickly pass, and we fly away.
The answer is False. The psalm says those years “…quickly pass, and we fly away.” Fast, not slow. I used to think a drawer made time crawl, but Moses says life is quick.

The answer is True. The psalm says, “Your wrath matches the fear You are due.” It's a heavy line, and I think Moses means it to be. We've been in some serious verses, friends, and the prayer is about to turn.

The answer is to present a heart of wisdom! The prayer says, “So teach us to number our days, that we may present a heart of wisdom.” He doesn't ask to number days just to count them. The reason he gives is wisdom. That's a better reason than the one I had back in the junk drawer, where I counted the dust as it fell.
The answer is True. Moses prays, “Return, O LORD! How long will it be? Have compassion on Your servants.” After all those heavy verses, he asks for compassion. I think that's a good move.

The answer is His loving devotion! The prayer says, “Satisfy us in the morning with Your loving devotion…” That's what he asks for to start the day. Good thing too, because I'm not satisfied before my first batch of cookies.
The answer is False. Moses asks God to satisfy them “…that we may sing for joy and be glad all our days.” That's every day, not just one. I'd take that over a single good day any time.

The answer is afflicted. The prayer says, “Make us glad for as many days as You have afflicted us, for as many years as we have seen evil.” Moses is asking for gladness to match the hard days. It's a very honest prayer.

The answer is their children. The prayer says, “May Your work be shown to Your servants, and Your splendor to their children.” Moses is looking past his own generation. He asks that the next generation see God's splendor too.

The answer is the work of their hands! The prayer ends, “establish for us the work of our hands—yes, establish the work of our hands!” He asks it twice, friends. I'd say that's the part he really means.
